title: Finite tensor-kernel tests detect factorization when the cokernel is finitely presented
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $U,V,W$ be $R$-modules, and $f:U\to V$ and $g:U\to W$ be $R$-linear maps. Suppose the quotient $V/f(U)$, namely the cokernel of $f$, is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. If for every finitely presented $R$-module $Q$ one has $\ker(f\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_Q)\subseteq\ker(g\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_Q)$ as submodules of $U\otimes_RQ$, then there is an $R$-linear map $h:V\to W$ with $g=h\circ f$. Tensor products and their induced maps are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No finite-generation, flatness or injectivity hypothesis on $U,V,W$ or $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 059D, lemma-domination, combined with Tag 059C, lemma-domination-fp: finite-presentation tests suffice for domination, and domination implies factorization when the cokernel of f is finitely presented.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-module-pushout-quotient-presentation] to $(U,V,W,f,g)$; rename its $(E,\pi,j,k)$ as $(P,\rho,a,b)$. Thus $P=(W\oplus V)/\operatorname{im}(g,-f)$, $a(w)=\rho(w,0)$, $b(v)=\rho(0,v)$, $ag=bf$, and $\rho$ is surjective with kernel $\operatorname{im}(g,-f)$. Put $C=V/f(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Write $q:V\to C$ for its quotient map. Since $qf=0=0g$, the stated universal property induces $p:P\to C$ from $0:W\to C$ and $q$, with $pa=0$, $pb=q$ and $p(\rho(w,v))=[v]$. It is surjective since $p(b(v))=[v]$. Every element of $P$ has a representative $\rho(w,v)$. If $p(\rho(w,v))=0$, write $v=f(u)$; then $\rho(w,v)=\rho(w,f(u))=\rho(w+g(u),0)=a(w+g(u))$, since $\rho(g(u),-f(u))=0$. Conversely $pa=0$, so $\ker p=a(W)$. The hypothesis makes $C$ finitely presented.

source.place: Tags 0AUM and 059D: explicit pushout and cokernel.

proof.text: For a finitely presented test module $T$, apply [lem-trf-quotient-pair-tensor-kernel] with its $(P,Q,Q',E,L)=(U,V,W,P,T)$ and $(a,b,\pi,j)=(f,g,\rho,a)$. Step 1 supplies surjectivity, the kernel equality and $j=\pi\iota_1$. It gives $\ker(a\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)=(g\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(\ker(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_T))$. Each element is $(g\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(z)$ with $(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(z)=0$; the assumed kernel containment for this same $T$ makes it zero. Thus $a\otimes\mathrm{id}_T$ is injective for every finitely presented $T$.

source.place: Tag 0AUM: tensor-kernel computation, for the finitely presented tests of Tag 059C.

proof.text: The swaps $M\otimes_RQ\to Q\otimes_RM$, $m\otimes q\mapsto q\otimes m$, come from the bilinear universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Composing with the reverse swap sends $m\otimes q$ to $q\otimes m$ and back to $m\otimes q$; the other composite likewise fixes every pure tensor. Generation makes both composites identities. The two maps $\sigma_P(a\otimes1)$ and $(1\otimes a)\sigma_W$ both send $w\otimes q$ to $q\otimes a(w)$; generation by pure tensors gives their equality on the whole tensor product. Step 2 therefore makes $1_Q\otimes a$ injective for each finitely presented $Q$. [lem-trf-universal-injective-finite-test] gives injectivity of $1_Q\otimes a$ for every $Q$; conjugating by the same swaps gives injectivity of $a\otimes1_Q$ for every $Q$. For $Q=R$, if $a(w)=0$, injectivity of $a\otimes1_R$ gives $w\otimes1=0$. Applying the linear map $W\otimes_RR\to W$, $w\otimes r\mapsto rw$, obtained from the bilinear universal property, gives $w=0$. Thus $a$ is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] to the exact sequence from step 1: its hypothesis is precisely $\ker p=a(W)$ and surjectivity of $p$. It gives exactness at $P\otimes_RQ$ and surjectivity onto $C\otimes_RQ$ for every $Q$. Hence $0\to W\xrightarrow{a}P\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$ is universally exact.

source.place: Tag 058K (theorem-universally-exact-criteria), finite tests; Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), right exactness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-universally-exact-fp-split] with $(A,B,C,i,p)=(W,P,V/f(U),a,p)$. Step 1 gives surjectivity and kernel equality; the original hypothesis gives finite presentation of $C$; step 3 gives injectivity and universal exactness. Obtain a linear map $r:P\to W$ with $ra=\mathrm{id}_W$. Set $h=rb:V\to W$. The relation $bf=ag$ from step 1 gives $hf=rbf=rag=g$.
